title: Norovirus & Sickness Reporting
blurb: Why sickness and diarrhoea mean staying off food work, why soap beats gel, and how to clean up sickness properly.
siteNotes: Who to call and how to report sickness before a shift
The venue's sickness clean-up kit, where it is kept and what disinfectant it contains
Who confirms staff are clear to return to food work after 48 hours symptom-free
legalNotes: From BHB-10MT-55. Food handlers must report illness and stay off food work: Food Safety and Hygiene (England) Regulations 2013 and Regulation (EC) 852/2004 Annex II, chapter VIII; FSA guidance is 48 hours symptom-free.
CHECK: the trainer says alcohol gel does not reliably kill norovirus, which matches NHS and FSA advice; confirm the venue sickness policy matches.

cards.kicker: All food and guest-facing teams · 10 minutes
cards.title: Norovirus & Sickness Reporting
cards.body:
By the end of this session you can:
- explain how norovirus spreads
- report sickness and stay off food work
- clean up sickness safely

cards.title: Spreads like wildfire
cards.body:
Norovirus, sometimes called the "winter vomiting bug", is extremely contagious. It takes only a tiny number of virus particles to make someone ill.

One unwell food handler can infect dozens of guests.

cards.title: Sick? Stay off food work
cards.body:
The single most important rule: if you have sickness or diarrhoea, do NOT come to work with food, and report it to your manager.

You must be symptom-free for at least 48 hours before you return to handling food.

items.title: Sickness or diarrhoea
items.text: Do not come in to handle food.

cards.title: It can feel that way, but...
cards.body: It can feel like you are letting the team down. Coming in could shut us down and make guests seriously ill.

left.title: Do
items: Stay off food until 48 hours clear

cards.title: Soap and warm water
cards.body:
Handwashing is your best defence. Alcohol hand gels do NOT reliably kill norovirus. Wash thoroughly with soap and warm water.

> Gel is a top-up, not a substitute, especially when norovirus is around.

left.title: Do
items: Wash with soap and warm water

cards.title: Clean it promptly and properly
cards.body: If someone is sick on the premises, clean it up promptly.

items.title: Disinfectant
items.text: One that is effective against viruses.

cards.title: Remember
cards.body:
- Sickness or diarrhoea: do not handle food, and report it
- Be symptom-free for 48 hours before returning to food
- Alcohol gel does not reliably kill norovirus: wash with soap and warm water
- Clean up sickness promptly with PPE and a virus-effective disinfectant
- Clean a wide area, dispose safely and wash your hands

cards.why: It takes only a tiny number of virus particles to make someone ill.

cards.q: You have had sickness or diarrhoea. How long must you be symptom-free before handling food again?
cards.why: You must be symptom-free for at least 48 hours before you return to handling food.

cards.q: Alcohol hand gel reliably kills norovirus on its own.
cards.why: Alcohol hand gels do not reliably kill norovirus. Gel is a top-up, not a substitute.

cards.q: What is the best way to clean your hands against norovirus?
options: Hand gel rubbed in until dry
A quick rinse under cold water
Wash thoroughly with soap and warm water
cards.why: Wash thoroughly with soap and warm water.

cards.q: You have sickness and diarrhoea before a shift. You should:
options: Come in as normal and avoid the kitchen
Report it and stay off food work
Come in and just wear gloves
Come in and wash your hands often
cards.why: Report it to your manager and do not come to work with food.

cards.q: One unwell food handler can infect many guests.
cards.why: One unwell food handler can infect dozens of guests.

cards.q: Which is an item of PPE to wear when cleaning up vomit?
cards.why: Wear the correct PPE: gloves and apron.

cards.q: When cleaning up sickness you should clean:
options: The whole floor of the building
A wide area around the spot
cards.why: Clean a wide area around the spot.

cards.q: Norovirus can spread through hands, surfaces, food and the air.
cards.why: It spreads through contaminated hands, surfaces, food and even the air after someone has been sick.

cards.q: You should use a disinfectant that is effective against viruses.
cards.why: Use the right disinfectant that is effective against viruses.
